significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a knowledge readout is approximately a conjunction of independently measurable belief and truth coordinates—“knowledge activation ~ min(belief, truth)”—and that departures from this relation predict factivity failures; this is a form-(iii) functional and predictive coupling, supplemented by a causal mechanistic claim. It would fix expected internal responses across the belief/truth combinations and explain a behavioral phenomenon, rather than merely establish that epistemic information is decodable; Marks and Tegmark’s Geometry of Truth and Li et al.’s ITI make the availability and causal relevance of truth-related activation signals concrete reference points for why this decomposition would constrain subsequent explanations. A false result would meaningfully reject the simple conjunction account, although it would not by itself distinguish an independent knowledge representation from lexical or other entangled alternatives; true and false are distinguishable despite “approximately” leaving the numerical tolerance underspecified. Topic-substitution check: generic research on LLM beliefs would not imply this specific conjunction law or its link to factivity errors, so the score is supported by claim-specific content rather than the topic’s importance.

reach.justification: The clearest handle is “a diagnostic for which of the three axes a given model has failed to separate,” operationally accompanied by conjunction strength and the proposed belief/truth steering axes. Because the claim says conjunction breakdowns “predict exactly the factivity failures,” the diagnostic can be used ex ante to forecast a model’s failure profile before deployment, although it does not directly supply a model-design or training rule. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a relation—knowledge should respond most strongly when both belief and truth are positive, and cleaner conjunction should accompany higher factivity accuracy—rather than merely as a procedure for finding an unconstrained direction; the asserted scope is cross-model LLM comparison, with likely uptake by interpretability researchers and model auditors. Topic-substitution check: deleting the three-axis geometry leaves no diagnostic, predictor, or transferable conjunction relation, so this reach does not come merely from the broad LLM-belief topic.
